key_insight: CARV (Compute-Aware, Variance-accounting) reduces the expensive Monte Carlo variance coming from frozen diffusion teachers by explicitly measuring where variance arises (across noise levels and samples) and allocating compute hierarchically to those high-variance components, cutting required upstream work.
problem_solved: Downstream pipelines that consume gradients from pretrained diffusion teachers (e.g., text-to-3D, single-step distillation, data attribution) rely on Monte Carlo expectations over noise levels and Gaussian samples; estimator variance dominates compute cost because each sample requires expensive upstream rendering/simulation/encoding.
method: Estimate variance contributions across noise levels and Gaussian noise draws to identify where sampling yields the largest estimator variance.
Allocate a fixed compute budget adaptively and hierarchically—spending more samples where variance is highest and fewer where it is low (compute-aware sampling).
Combine hierarchical/stratified sampling and variance-reduction constructs (e.g., control variates or correlated estimators) to lower sample complexity per downstream gradient estimate.
impact: Significantly lowers the compute and wall-clock cost of pipelines that rely on frozen diffusion teachers, enabling faster iteration, cheaper model distillation and attribution, and more practical deployment of expensive upstream simulators or renderers.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: frozen diffusion teacher → sampling loop → expensive renderer/encoder → downstream consumer (text-to-3D/distillation), with MC samples highlighted.
Variance heatmap across noise levels (x-axis: noise level, y-axis: variance contribution) showing where variance concentrates.
Compute-allocation bar chart comparing uniform sampling vs CARV's hierarchical allocation (same budget → lower variance).
Cost vs accuracy/variance plot showing reduced samples or compute to reach a target variance with CARV.
paper_title: Variance Reduction for Expectations with Diffusion Teachers
paper_authors: Jesse Bettencourt, Xindi Wu, Matan Atzmon, James Lucas, Jonathan Lorraine
